page.text:
A *predicate* is an incomplete statement containing one or more open
variables. On its own, an open expression such as '$x^2 < 2$' or '$x$
divides $y$' is neither true nor false; it becomes a definite proposition
only when specific objects are substituted for its variables, or when
those variables are bound by quantifiers.

Crucially, every variable in mathematics belongs to an explicit or
implicit *universe of discourse* or *domain*. The statement '$x^2 = 2$'
has solutions if the domain of $x$ is the real numbers $\mathbb{R}$, but
has no solutions if the domain is restricted to the rational numbers
$\mathbb{Q}$. Specifying the domain is not an incidental detail; it is an
organic part of the predicate's definition.
